status: Partial D14 syscall-level fault characterization; does not establish D14 completion, G1, power-loss behavior, host qualification, or H1.

capturedSource.basis: A git archive of baseCommit plus only the untracked fsync fault test overlay.

test.name: TestSQLiteOwnerKernelFsyncFailure
test.faultMechanism: A fresh helper test process sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs a seccomp-BPF filter with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC. On AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64, the filter returns EIO only for SYS_FSYNC or SYS_FDATASYNC when arg0 is the selected SQLite WAL fd; other syscalls are allowed. TSYNC return status is checked, and /proc/self/status Seccomp_filters changes from 0 to 1 in each injected case.
test.targetFdDiscovery: The helper scans /proc/self/fd, requires an exact readlink path match, and confirms the target inode and device with fstat before arming the filter.
test.arming: Each fault is installed only after the owner and protected-root reservation is verified durable and after a local O_EXCL effect marker is written and fsynced exactly once. The owner-WAL hook runs after the second successful VerifyTerminalEffectOwner and immediately before the owner terminal write. The protected-root hook runs immediately before entering CompareAndSwapTerminalCheckpoint; the injected root-WAL syscall error occurred during the protected clock high-water commit in terminal CAS verification, before the terminal anchor CAS transaction was committed.
test.effect: The effect is a local test marker; terminal Store/admission pins and the verifier are synthetic. No provider call, secret, VM action, or production RunEffect integration was exercised.

cases.name: owner-wal-fsync
cases.syscallEvidence: The exact owner-WAL fd received seccomp EIO and SQLite returned extended code 1034 (SQLITE_IOERR_FSYNC), primary code 10. errors.As reaches the typed modernc SQLite error. The owner was poisoned and the protected root was not.
cases.freshProcessResult: After process exit the owner database exposed a local terminal head despite the failed sync. The fresh root still authenticated the exact reservation, so LoadCheckpoint rejected the unanchored terminal head with ErrRollback. The retry path was rejected and second_effect_callbacks remained 0. This EIO result differs from the prior RLIMIT_FSIZE/EFBIG characterization, which recovered the exact pending reservation.

cases.name: protected-root-wal-fsync
cases.syscallEvidence: The exact protected-root WAL fd received seccomp EIO and the returned error text includes disk I/O error (1034), SQLITE_IOERR_FSYNC. The owner and root were poisoned in the fault process. The SQLite error is formatted through the existing terminal-CAS wrapper, so errors.As does not recover its typed driver error and ErrOwnerStore identity is not preserved by that wrapper.
cases.freshProcessResult: The local terminal owner head was not authenticated by the root. A fresh process verified the root still held the reservation digest, observed ErrRollback from LoadCheckpoint, and confirmed the raw owner row held the terminal outcome. The retry path was rejected and second_effect_callbacks remained 0.

cases.name: unfiltered-positive-control
cases.syscallEvidence: No seccomp filter was installed; Seccomp_filters remained 0 to 0. Normal SQLite terminal persistence completed.
cases.freshProcessResult: A separate process reopened the owner and protected root and verified the terminal checkpoint was root-anchored.

test.freshProcessVerification: Each fault helper exited before a separate helper process reopened the databases. Both actual EIO cases produced an unanchored terminal owner head that the protected root rejected; neither case exposed a second effect callback.

limitations: The EIO results are induced at the Linux syscall boundary by seccomp. They are not physical media failures, filesystem ENOSPC, power loss, or evidence of persistence behavior across an actual machine crash.

The results characterize SQLite owner and protected-root error paths only. They do not complete D14, establish G1 or H1, or qualify a host, filesystem, platform, deployment, provider, or real external effect.
The protected-root case faults its clock high-water SQLite WAL commit during terminal CAS verification. It does not claim the terminal anchor CAS transaction itself reached its commit fsync.
